clue.text: Guard taking action to provide protection for old-timer

parts.note: to guard is to keep watch, or a watch is a guard on duty
a case is a legal action brought in court

explanation.surface: A sentry takes legal steps to shield an elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-timer' looks like an elderly person, but it is read as a timepiece, something that keeps time.
explanation.definitionFit: A casing protects the mechanism of a timepiece, here cheekily called an old-timer.

clue.text: German runner getting stitch again when climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to resew is to stitch a second time

explanation.surface: A German athlete has to have a torn kit repaired while going uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is crossword shorthand for a river; the Weser flows through northern Germany to the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a runner in crossword language, and this one flows across northern Germany.

clue.text: Daily newspaper over a pound? Thus price increases appear novel

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily tabloid
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
so means thus, in that way
rises are increases, as in price rises

explanation.surface: A tabloid costing over a pound suggests prices are rising unusually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' just stacks the pieces in a down clue; 'novel' looks like an adjective for unusual but is the definition. The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Ernest Hemingway's 1926 book about expatriates at a Pamplona fiesta.

clue.text: Rider in storm nears home shortly

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the letters are tossed into a new order
cut short means the last letter of the word home is lopped off

explanation.surface: A cyclist battling through a tempest is nearly back at the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims HOME to HOM; 'in storm' shuffles NEARS with HOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider on horseback is a horseman, a general synonym.

clue.text: In a stage musical, criminally treat versatile performers

indicators.note: one piece placed in another: the theft goes inside the show's name

parts.note: Cats is Andrew Lloyd Webber's long-running stage musical
to rob someone is to treat them criminally

explanation.surface: In a West End show, cast members behave badly toward talented performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumblers and trapeze artists are agile, versatile entertainers in a circus.

clue.text: In part of EU once elected representative's held sway

indicators.note: has held, so the old country name keeps the politician inside it

parts.note: Eire is the old name used for Ireland, a member of the EU
MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the European Union, a politician once wielded power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only sets the scene; Ireland's Irish name was the usual English name for the state in mid-century, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway means rule or dominion, and an empire is the realm or power a ruler holds.

clue.text: Shock as saint enters church property?

indicators.note: goes inside, so the saint's letter is put into the hair

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it, like a mane

explanation.surface: Alarm as a holy figure walks into a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as fright but means a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's house owned by the church, especially in Scotland, is a church property.

clue.text: Male reluctant ultimately to enter exam? One's only human

indicators.note: going in, so the chosen letter is placed inside the spoken exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of reluctant is used

explanation.surface: A man unwilling to sit his oral test admits he is only human.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mortal, subject to death, is what makes someone merely human.

clue.text: Conscription possibly viewed as antisocial? Never

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Being called up for the army might seem antisocial, but no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals a rearrangement of ANTISOCIAL plus NEVER. Britain had compulsory military service until 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory military service for young men, as in post-war Britain, is a form of conscription.

clue.text: Government department keeping queen in comfort no longer

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the queen goes within comfort

parts.note: to cheer someone is to comfort them

explanation.surface: A ministry holds on to a monarch no longer at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse of clue order: EX from 'no longer' leads.
explanation.definitionFit: The British treasury department that manages public revenue is so named after a chequered counting table.

clue.text: One's contemptuous about ecology party, no good in revolution

indicators.note: turned round, so the whole string is read from the back

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: no good means G, for good, is dropped

parts.note: the Greens are the environmentalist party

explanation.surface: A scornful critic attacks the environmentalists as useless rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' drops G from GREENS, leaving REENS; 'in revolution' turns RE + REENS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sneers is a person showing contempt.

clue.text: Single despicable character in film such as Hook?

indicators.note: placed inside, so the two pieces sit in the movie

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: One villain dominates a movie like the swashbuckling Hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hook' looks like a film title, but it is Captain Hook of Peter Pan, so the definition describes him as buccaneering.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Hook is a buccaneer, so anyone like him is pirate-like in character.

clue.text: Tour in resort, taking eastern direction

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday trip in a seaside resort heads east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a course or way taken, a sense of direction.

clue.text: Grumble about a part song

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the complaint word is read backwards

parts.note: to crab is to grumble or complain
a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: Someone complains about one bit of a choral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part song' looks like a phrase, a song for several voices, but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarole is a Venetian gondolier's song, or music in its rhythm.

clue.text: Feature of Indian cuisine fellow finds almost Greek

parts.note: a chap is a fellow

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Attic means Greek, from Attica around Athens

explanation.surface: A man discovers that Indian food is nearly as good as Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat unleavened bread is a staple served with Indian meals.

clue.text: Priest officiating in church needing to get support in fast

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: placed inside the period of fasting

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
a bra is a support garment

explanation.surface: A clergyman leading church services needs backing during the fasting season.
explanation.definitionFit: The priest who conducts a service, especially the Eucharist, is its celebrant.

clue.text: United striker overturned ban

indicators.note: turned over, so both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
a bat is something you strike a ball with

explanation.surface: A Manchester United forward has his suspension reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer but is a cricket bat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant spelling of taboo, a prohibition.

clue.text: Fellow consumer turned up in party at pub with air conditioning

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the string is read bottom to top

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Another diner arrives at a party held in an air-conditioned pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow consumer' reads as another shopper but is one who eats his fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal consumes others of its own kind, hence a consumer of fellows.

clue.text: Name of German boy band fronted by lady-killer

indicators.note: fronted by means the second piece goes in front of the first

parts.note: a wolf is a womaniser
a gang is a band of people

explanation.surface: The name of a German boy band led by a heart-throb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy band' looks like a pop group but splits across definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common German masculine first name, as in Mozart.

clue.text: Girl's not extremely sophisticated

indicators.note: not at the extremes, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: classy means stylish, sophisticated

explanation.surface: A young woman claims she is not very refined.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a mainly Scottish and northern English word for a young woman.

clue.text: Driver perhaps drinks nothing — unlike me?

indicators.note: takes in, so the zero is swallowed inside

parts.note: a car user is a driver, for example
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A motorist touches no alcohol, quite unlike the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The teetotal driver is the wordplay; the setter jokes that he is no such abstainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveller drinking heavily is the opposite of an abstainer, so the self-effacing setter's opposite.

clue.text: See friend swallowing drug for depression

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the drug goes within friend

parts.note: an ally is a friend
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Watch your mate taking pills to beat the blues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' reads as low mood but is a dip in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley is a low area between hills, a depression in the ground.

clue.text: Some engaged in 7 remain unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Some of those called up stay restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the answer to 7 down, national service, in which many served in the air force.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the air force were among the conscripts doing compulsory service.

clue.text: Islander's cruel remark wounding Diana

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark

indicators.note: wounding means damaging, so the name's letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A Caribbean man's spiteful comment hurts Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Barbados in the Caribbean is an islander.

clue.text: Fail resit? Here are the odds, to begin with

indicators.note: odds means the odd-numbered letters, one, three, five and so on, of the two preceding words

explanation.surface: A student who flunked a retake hears the betting at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds' looks like betting prices but means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: First, as an adverb, means initially, at the outset.

clue.text: Cross borne by Antigone

indicators.note: carried by, so the answer sits inside the name

explanation.surface: Antigone bears her cross, as Greek tragedy demands.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the cross between a male tiger and a lioness, a hybrid.

clue.text: David's boy, a born dancer with no end of aptitude

indicators.note: without, so the chosen letter is removed from the dancer

parts.note: Salome danced for Herod, in the Bible

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of aptitude

explanation.surface: David's son, a natural dancer, has no talent at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Absalom was King David's rebellious son in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Trying to stop family members taking part in card game

indicators.note: going into, so relatives are placed inside the card game

parts.note: brag is a card game like poker
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Relatives join a card game, then try to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Braking is slowing a vehicle, trying to halt it.

clue.text: Like a match, perhaps, likely to flare up?

definitions.meaning: test-like, as a cricket Test match is
irritable, quick to lose one's temper

explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket match; 'flare up' keeps the match-striking picture going.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means irritable, and cheekily Test-y means resembling a Test match.

clue.text: Colour of duck, say, on easternmost edges of Lake Michigan

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, nil
e.g. means say, for example
re means on, concerning
the eastern, right-hand ends of the words Lake and Michigan are their final letters

explanation.surface: What colour is a duck seen on the eastern shore of a great lake?
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like a bird but is cricket's zero score; 'easternmost edges' means the right-hand end of each word, as east is right on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile green is a pale bluish-green shade, named after the river's waters.
